input.rationale: Completes the sparse-trim finding with its protective counterpart: unlike trim, the snapshot path bounds compaction only by the local decided index and never consults the minimum accepted index, so a snapshot-capable entry type can still compact a sparse-pid configuration. Recorded as a source-level behavior so the defect account's scope (trim API, not all compaction) rests on a cited mechanism.

knowledge.statement: SequencePaxos::snapshot passes its index to InternalStorage::try_snapshot, which accepts any index less than the local decided index (equal maps to the decided index without the StopSign) and rejects only indices greater than decided with UndecidedIndex. It performs trim, compacted-index and snapshot writes atomically and never consults the minimum accepted index. The snapshot API is therefore not affected by the sparse-pid placeholders that block trim, so a snapshot-capable Entry type can still compact a configuration such as {1,2,5}.
knowledge.conditions: A snapshot-capable Entry type (Snapshot::use_snapshots() true) and a snapshot index not greater than the node's decided index; the node may be a follower when local_only is true.

knowledge.statement: Pending append_notify calls in the runtime actor are resolved in this order: Ok(idx) when the recorded assignment index is <= the actor's current decided index; Superseded when the assignment ballot is lower than the current promise ballot; Timeout when the deadline passed; otherwise the pending stays queued. The Ok arm is evaluated first and does not inspect the log or compare the entry stored at idx.
knowledge.conditions: omnipaxos_runtime actor, append_notify tracking enabled; pending entry has an assigned (idx, ballot) from local accept or a remote Assigned reply; drain_notifiers runs on each actor tick and after command handling.

knowledge.statement: The runtime's test suite treats a successful append_notify as a claim that the caller's entry is decided at the returned index: the batching regression test reads the decided log back and asserts the value at the returned index equals the submitted entry, so a returned index holding a different value is a contract violation under the project's own expectation.
knowledge.conditions: The test environment's exercised conditions: 3-node runtime cluster with real transport, batching enabled, and a submitted append_notify entry; this is an individual test expectation plus the handle-level description, not a proof of a defect by itself.

knowledge.statement: The Superseded regression test demonstrates that an entry accepted only on the old leader can be genuinely lost and replaced at the same log index by a different value under the new leader, and that Superseded is the intended observable in that case; it also shows the origin node learns of the new higher-ballot leader.
knowledge.conditions: 3-node runtime cluster, the elected leader's outgoing traffic is cut while its incoming traffic stays open; a new leader is elected by the other two nodes and a fresh entry is appended and decided at the old index.

knowledge.statement: With decided=6 and compacted=4 on the executed two-node log, read_decided_suffix(1) returned exactly [Trimmed(4), Decided(5), Decided(6)] (len 3) although decided-from is 5, while read_decided_suffix(4) returned [Decided(5), Decided(6)] (len 2). The trimmed prefix is represented by a single Trimmed element, so the returned vector length is not the number of requested log indices when the start is below the compacted index.
knowledge.conditions: Two OmniPaxos instances (pids 1,2) built from ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2]}, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots; node 1 becomes leader via try_become_leader, appends Value(1..=6) with full message delivery after each append, then trims to 4 and the trim is forwarded to node 2; both nodes report decided 6.

knowledge.statement: Applied to those real read_decided_suffix outputs, one cursor step per returned element (the actor's push_to_sub rule) leaves next_idx at 4 after the catch-up from 1, and the next push_to_all_subs read from 4 yields entries 5 and 6 again, so the delivered value sequence is 5,6,5,6 with duplicates of 5 and 6 while decided remains 6 and no new entry was decided.
knowledge.conditions: Same executed setup as @suffix_collapse_observed; the cursor replay reproduces omnipaxos_runtime/src/actor.rs push_to_sub (next_idx += 1 per element) and one subsequent push_to_all_subs read from the resulting cursor (start = 0 for a single subscriber). The replay is a reconstruction of the runtime source logic over executed core outputs, not an execution of the runtime crate.

knowledge.statement: On the executed five-node run, node 5 had decided through index 5 and read index 4 as Decided(Value(5)); after the new leader's AcceptSync it reported decided 4 and read index 4 as Undecided(Value(5)); after the new leader re-decided index 5 it reported decided 5 and read index 4 as Decided(Value(5)) again. The same log index was therefore observed Decided, Undecided and Decided with unchanged value.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances (pids 1..5), ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2,3,4,5]}, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots. Entry 5 is accepted by 1,2,3,5 and decided by leader 1, but the Decide reaches only node 5; nodes 2 and 3 stay decided 4 with accepted 5. Node 1 is then cut, node 2 is elected with promises from 3 and 4 only (decided 4), and node 5's Prepare is delivered only after node 2 is in Accept, so its Promise is handled by handle_promise_accept and answered with an AcceptSync carrying decided 4.

knowledge.statement: A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum (handle_majority_promises -> get_max_decided_idx). A follower whose Promise arrives after that quorum is answered by handle_promise_accept with send_accsync stamped with the leader's current decided index, and handle_acceptsync passes that value to sync_log, which assigns it to the decided index without comparing it to the follower's existing value. A follower that had already learned a later decision therefore loses decided progress until the new leader re-accepts and re-decides the entry.
knowledge.conditions: Majority quorum with five nodes; at least one member of the new leader's prepare quorum accepted the entry without deciding it; the more-informed follower is delayed past the quorum; no snapshots involved in the sync.

knowledge.statement: With a single lost Prepare and the public reconnected(2) call, node 5's decided index fell from 5 to 4 and read(4) changed from Decided(Value(5)) to Undecided(Value(5)) after the new leader's Accept-phase AcceptSync; after the new leader re-decided index 5, node 5 returned to decided 5 and Decided(Value(5)). The observed message sequence was PrepareReq from node 5, Prepare to node 5, Promise from node 5, AcceptSync to node 5 and an Accepted reply, with lost_prepare_count 1.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances (pids 1..5), MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots. Entry 5 is decided by leader 1 with nodes 1,2,3,5 accepting but the Decide reaching only node 5; node 2 is elected with promises from 3 and 4 (decided 4); the Prepare addressed to node 5 is dropped; the probe calls node5.reconnected(2) as the documented re-establish-connection entry point.

knowledge.statement: Entries appended while this node is leader in Phase::Prepare are pushed to buffered_proposals. When the node later receives an AcceptSync (after promising a leader, whether in the prepare phase or in the accept phase), handle_acceptsync calls forward_buffered_proposals before switching to Phase::Accept; that call takes the whole buffer and forwards it to the current leader if there is no accepted StopSign. The buffered entries are therefore re-proposed rather than stranded when leadership moves away before the prepare quorum completes.
knowledge.conditions: SequencePaxos with no accepted StopSign; the node promises a subsequent leader and receives its AcceptSync; the forwarded ProposalForward is delivered to that leader (normal message delivery).

knowledge.statement: On the executed three-node configuration {1,2,5} with three decided entries and all_accepted_min 3, trim(Some(2)) returned NotAllDecided(0), the compacted index stayed 0, and a following trim(None) also left the compacted index at 0 while returning Ok.
knowledge.conditions: Three OmniPaxos instances pids 1, 2 and 5, ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2,5]}, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots; node 1 elected with try_become_leader; three entries appended and fully delivered so every node reports decided 3 and accepted 3.

materials.text:
- `Decided(T)`: The entry is decided and guaranteed to not be reverted. It is thus safe to apply a decided entry to the application state. For instance, in our case, it is safe to update our key-value store when we read a `Decided(KeyValue)` entry.
- `Undecided(T)`: The entry is NOT decided and might be removed from the log at a later time. However, it could be useful in applications that allow speculative execution for example.

Recorded as a source-level behavior with two new anchors plus the trim-check anchor, keeping the trim defect's scope precise (trim API, not compaction in general). All four defect accounts and the earlier buffered-proposal protection remain unchanged.
